arxiv-2205-11536.title: Implications of a Temperature Dependent IMF I: Photometric Template Fitting
arxiv-2205-11536.creator: Albert Sneppen, Charles L. Steinhardt, Hagan Hensley, Adam S. Jermyn, Basel Mostafa, John R. Weaver
arxiv-2205-11536.description: Abstract A universal stellar initial mass function (IMF) should not be expected from theoretical models of star formation, but little conclusive observational evidence for a variable IMF has been uncovered. In this paper, a parameterization of the IMF is introduced into photometric template fitting of the COSMOS2015 catalog.

arxiv-2305-18840.title: Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions
arxiv-2305-18840.creator: Joseph Enguehard
arxiv-2305-18840.description: Abstract Explaining predictions based on multivariate time series data carries the additional difficulty of handling not only multiple features, but also time dependencies. It matters not only what happened, but also when, and the same feature could have a very different impact on a prediction depending on this time information.

arxiv-2311-13679.title: Parity vs. AC 0 with simple quantum preprocessing
arxiv-2311-13679.creator: Joseph Slote
arxiv-2311-13679.description: Abstract A recent line of work [ 5 , 27 , 12 , 6 , 28 ] has shown the unconditional advantage of constant-depth quantum computation, or 𝖰𝖭𝖢 𝟢 \mathsf{QNC^{0}} , over 𝖭𝖢 𝟢 \mathsf{NC^{0}} , 𝖠𝖢 𝟢 \mathsf{AC^{0}} , and related models of classical computation.

arxiv-2406-01002.title: Random Subspace Local Projections Thanks: Viet.Dinh@monash.edu , Didier.Nibbering@monash.edu , and Benjamin.Wong@monash.edu . Thanks: We thank the editor, three anonymous referees, Silvia Gonçalves, Eleonora Granziera, Luke Hartigan, Òscar Jordà, Daniel Lewis, Adrian Pagan, Barbara Rossi and partici
arxiv-2406-01002.creator: Viet Hoang Dinh, Didier Nibbering, Benjamin Wong
arxiv-2406-01002.description: Abstract We show how random subspace methods can be adapted to estimating local projections with many controls. Random subspace methods have their roots in the machine learning literature and are implemented by averaging over regressions estimated over different combinations of subsets of these controls.

arxiv-2406-12037.title: C/O Ratios and the formation of wide separation exoplanets Facilities: ALMA, NOEMA
arxiv-2406-12037.creator: Edwin A. Bergin, Richard A. Booth, Maria Jose Colmenares, John D. Ilee
arxiv-2406-12037.description: Abstract The gas and solid-state C/O ratios provide context to potentially link the atmospheric composition of planets to that of the natal disk. We provide a synthesis of extant estimates of the gaseous C/O and C/H ratios in planet-forming disks obtained primarily through analysis of Atacama Large Millimeter Array observations.

arxiv-2407-09911.title: SensEmo: Enabling Affective Learning through Real-time Emotion Recognition with Smartwatches
arxiv-2407-09911.creator: Kushan Choksi 1 , Hongkai Chen 2 , Karan Joshi 1 , Sukrutha Jade 1 , Shahriar Nirjon 3 , and Shan Lin 1
arxiv-2407-09911.description: Abstract Recent research has demonstrated the capability of physiological signals to infer both user emotional and attention responses. This presents an opportunity for leveraging widely available physiological sensors in smartwatches, to detect real-time emotional cues in users, such as stress and excitement. In this paper, we introduce SensEmo, a smartwatch-based system designed for affective learning.

arxiv-2410-09739.title: Fokker-Planck Central Moment Lattice Boltzmann Method for Effective Simulations of Fluid Dynamics
arxiv-2410-09739.creator: William Schupbach, Kannan Premnath
arxiv-2410-09739.description: Abstract We present a new formulation of the central moment lattice Boltzmann (LB) method based on a minimal continuous Fokker-Planck (FP) kinetic model, originally proposed for stochastic diffusive-drift processes (e.g., Brownian dynamics), by adapting it as a collision model for the continuous Boltzmann equation (CBE) for fluid dynamics.

arxiv-2503-18462.title: PALATE: Peculiar Application of the Law of Total Expectation to Enhance the Evaluation of Deep Generative Models
arxiv-2503-18462.creator: Tadeusz Dziarmaga *, Marcin Kądziołka, Laura Musioł, Patryk Marszałek, Artur Kasymov, Piotr Kościelniak, Marcin Mazur *, † \dagger
arxiv-2503-18462.description: Abstract Deep generative models (DGMs) have caused a paradigm shift in the field of machine learning, yielding noteworthy advancements in domains such as image synthesis, natural language processing, and other related areas. However, a comprehensive evaluation of these models that effectively captures the interplay among fidelity, diversity, and novelty in generated samples remains a persistent challenge.

arxiv-2601-18935.title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Ewens–Pitman random partition in the large- θ \theta regime via a martingale approach
arxiv-2601-18935.creator: B. Bercu, C. Contardi, E. Dolera, S. Favaro
arxiv-2601-18935.description: Abstract The Ewens-Pitman model defines a distribution on random partitions of { 1 , … , n } \{1,\ldots,n\} , with parameters α ∈ [ 0 , 1 ) \alpha\in[0,1) and θ > − α \theta>-\alpha ; the case α = 0 \alpha=0 reduces to the classical Ewens model from population genetics.

arxiv-2602-18271.title: Two-Stage Multiple Test Procedures Controlling False Discovery Rate with auxiliary variable and their Application to Set4 Δ \Delta Mutant Data
arxiv-2602-18271.creator: Seohwa Hwang, Mark Louie Ramos, DoHwan Park, Junyong Park, Johan Lim, Erin Green
arxiv-2602-18271.description: Abstract In this paper, we present novel methodologies that incorporate auxiliary variables for multiple hypotheses testing related to the main point of interest while effectively controlling the false discovery rate. When dealing with multiple tests concerning the primary variable of interest, researchers can use auxiliary variables to set preconditions for the significance of primary variables, thereby enhancing test efficacy.

pmc-11493284.title: 3D CNN for neuropsychiatry: Predicting Autism with interpretable Deep Learning applied to minimally preprocessed structural MRI data
pmc-11493284.creator: Mélanie Garcia, Clare Kelly, Francesca Benuzzi, Yangsong Zhang, Yangsong Zhang, Yangsong Zhang
pmc-11493284.description: Predictive modeling approaches are enabling progress toward robust and reproducible brain-based markers of neuropsychiatric conditions by leveraging the power of multivariate analyses of large datasets. While deep learning (DL) offers another promising avenue to further advance progress, there are challenges related to implementation in 3D (best for MRI) and interpretability.

pmc-12664140.title: Primary cilium and TULP3-dependent ciliary targeting of ACE2 in SARS-CoV-2 tropism
pmc-12664140.creator: Yun Hong Du, Wai Lam Tung, Ho Hoi Wu, Xuewen Hong, Alexis Shiying Huang, Run Huang, Zecheng Zhang, Qian-Yuan Tang, Bor Luen Tang, Xing-Lou Yang, Ruklanthi de Alwis, Chee Wah Tan, Catherine Hong Huan Hor
pmc-12664140.description: BackgroundViruses initiate infection by engaging specific receptors on the host cell surface. While the surface receptor ACE2 mediates SARS-CoV-2 entry, the precise role of subcellular trafficking, particularly, the exact involvement of primary cilium trafficking in viral entry remains largely unresolved.MethodsWe used in-vitro human cell models and SARS-CoV-2 pseudoviruses to elucidate the viral attachment and host cell entry mechanisms.

pmc-13156255.title: Psychometric properties and validation of short health literacy screening (SHLS) to identify low health literacy
pmc-13156255.creator: Sulmaz Ghahramani, Marzieh Rahimi, Majid Khadem-Rezaiyan, Mina Zarei, Mohammad Sayari, Ali Ardekani, Kamran Bagheri Lankarani
pmc-13156255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the psychometric properties and performance of the short health literacy screening (SHLS) to identify people with low health literacy among a set of Iranian adults in Mashhad and Shiraz.Methods: In this cross-sectional study, participants were 18-65 years old Iranian adults randomly selected from two major cities of Iran, encompassing inpatients, outpatients, and healthy individuals. They completed the demographic, SHLS, and Health Literacy for Iranian Adults (HELIA) questionnaires. Psychometric properties of SHLS were evaluated.

pmc-13198558.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Upadacitinib vs. Other JAK Inhibitors in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Global Real-World Setting
pmc-13198558.creator: Peter C Taylor, Aditi Kadakia, Jack Milligan, Ana Romero, Oliver Howell, Pankaj A Patel, Sophie Barlow, Roberto Caporali
pmc-13198558.description: IntroductionThis study aimed to compare the real-world effectiveness of upadacitinib vs. other Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).MethodsData were extracted from the Adelphi RA Disease Specific Programme™ (DSP), a cross-sectional survey administered to rheumatologists and their patients in the EU, UK, Japan, Canada, and the US from July 2021 to February 2022.

pmc-13282787.title: Exploring Overlooked Mediators Linking Myocardial Infarction to Hematologic Malignancies

pmc-13381662.title: Saliva, urine, and anorectal swabs as viable alternatives to lesion swabs for molecular diagnosis of mpox
pmc-13381662.creator: Andrew Nsawotebba, Valeria Nakintu, Jonathan Kabazzi, Rodney Kisuule, Misaki Wayengera, Alisen Ayitewala, Caroline Makoha, Samuel Jefferson Mutyaba, Edward Kiyonga, Sulaiman Ikoba, Caroline Achola, Aloysious Ssemaganda, Isaac Ssewanyana, Susan Nabadda
pmc-13381662.description: Mpox diagnosis relies on lesion swabs, which are infeasible when lesions are absent or inaccessible, limiting case detection during outbreaks and surveillance in resource-limited settings. This cross-sectional paired diagnostic study evaluated saliva, anorectal swabs, and urine as alternatives to lesion swabs (the reference standard) at the Entebbe Isolation Unit during Uganda’s 2024–2025 clade 1b outbreak. Among 120 participants (52.

pmc-13480732.title: Recent Advances in Photocatalyst‐Driven Protein Labeling and Proximity Mapping
pmc-13480732.creator: Shinichi Sato, Kazuki Miura, Juki Nakao, Hiroyuki Nakamura
pmc-13480732.description: Photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling chemical reactivity with light, offering unique opportunities for spatial and temporal regulation. While visible‐light photocatalysis was originally developed in the context of small‐molecule synthesis, recent years have witnessed its rapid expansion into the selective modification of peptides and proteins under biologically compatible conditions.

pmc-13536406.title: Integrated analysis of single-cell and bulk RNA-sequence data reveal plasma dendritic cell-related diagnostic model for Sjögren’s syndrome based on machine learning
pmc-13536406.creator: Jinhao Zhang, Chunye Zhang, Huan Shi
pmc-13536406.description: Background/purposePlasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) play a critical role in linking innate and adaptive immunity in the pathogenesis of Sjögren’s syndrome (SS). This study aimed to characterize pDC functional features in SS by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data and to develop a pDC-related gene signature–based diagnostic model.

pmc-13632300.title: Assessing loneliness in later life: validation of the De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale for Portuguese older adults
pmc-13632300.creator: João Tavares, Oscar Ribeiro, Javier Yanguas Lezaun, Sofia Silva, Carolina Soares, Matilde Jóia-Gomes, Sara Guerra, Liliana Sousa
pmc-13632300.description: Assessing loneliness is essential to better understand older adults’ mental health needs and to inform timely and appropriate interventions. The De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale (DJGLS) is one of the most widely used measures of loneliness worldwide. However, there is no evidence regarding its psychometric adequacy for older adults in Portugal.
